description: Figure 2 is a bar chart illustrating five distinct layer grouping patterns applied across four groups, labeled G₁ through G₄, as indicated by the caption. The horizontal axis represents the group identifiers (G₁, G₂, G₃, G₄) in sequential order, while the vertical axis represents the number of layers within each group, with a linear scale. The chart visually depicts five different grouping strategies: (i) Increasing, where the number of layers in each subsequent group (Nᵢ₊₁) is greater than the previous (Nᵢ); (ii) Uniform, where the number of layers per group remains constant (Nᵢ₊₁ = Nᵢ); (iii) Decreasing, where the number of layers per group progressively reduces (Nᵢ₊₁ < Nᵢ); (iv) Spindle, characterized by a smaller number of layers at both ends (N₁ < N₂ = N₃ > N₄); and (v) Bottleneck, which features a larger number of layers at both ends (N₁ > N₂ = N₃ < N₄). Each pattern is represented by a single bar corresponding to its group designation on the horizontal axis, with the bar's height indicating the number of layers assigned to that group according to the specified pattern. The bars are arranged sequentially along the horizontal axis, and there is no visual indication of sorting or emphasis on any particular bar.
